To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aggregation of the isolated myofibrillar protein, S1, is determined by its denaturation at high ionic strength and by intermolecular interaction of its N–terminal extension with other S1 at low ionic strengths.

the thermal aggregation of myosin S1 is independent of the light chain isoform in the presence of ionic strength close to the physiological values, while at lower ionic strength the aggregation is strongly dependent on the light chain isoforms.

the aggregation of myosin subfragment-1 (S1) isoform containing light chain A1, which is the major light chain in vertebrate skeletal muscle myosin, is dependent on the S1 concentration and is not accompanied by the thermal denaturation of S1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the A1 isoform of the essential light chain in the thermally induced aggregation of myosin S1, as well as in the thermally activated aggregation of actomyosin.

the effects of the A1 and A2 light chains on the aggregation properties of myosin subfragment-1, and it is suggested that these light chains may play a role in the regulation of the myofilament lattice structure in muscle fibers.
the aggregation properties of the myosin head in its native and denatured states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of the N–terminally extended A1 light chain in S1 is not a sufficient condition for its aggregation at low ionic strengths, but it may be a necessary condition for the S1 aggregation at low temperatures.
the A1 isoform of the “essential” light chain is involved in the regulation of the aggregation of myosin molecules in the muscle fibers.
the aggregation properties and thermal stability of S1 containing the A1 light chains are different from those containing the A2 light chains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light chain A1 is not involved in the S1 aggregation at high ionic strength, while it may contribute to the S1 aggregation under conditions close to those in living muscle fibers.

the aggregation of the S1 isoform containing the A1 light chains (which is predominant in skeletal muscle) may be more pronounced in vivo than the S1 isoforms containing A2 light chains (predominant in smooth and cardiac muscles).

the myosin head containing a light chain (LC) A1 (but, not A2) has a higher aggregation propensity at low ionic strengths, which may result in the formation of aggregates of myosin heads at the low temperatures in the vicinity of the physiological temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N–terminal region of the A1 chain is able to bind to other S1 molecules at low ionic strenght, and this binding is independent of the S-1 denaturation.
myosin light chains can have significant influence on the aggregation properties of the S1 head.
the aggregation of the myosin head is a complex process involving both thermal denaturation and intermolecular interactions between the myosin heads.
